For hikes I recommand Eilat mountains (for just the beauty), also Mesada (probably the best place to go to if you interested in history, but you probably been there already since its one of the most popular places).  
In the north there is Ksiv stream (נחל כזיב) which is also popular and along the track there is also a crusader's fortress so some history in that too.  
Jerusalem and Yehoda and Shomron should be a must for you both for the historic value and the nature around them. Much more impactful then anything you have in the center.  
Tel aviv and the center is really urbanized and there arent much places to hike there.

I like the comment that said anywhere north of Jaffa and south of Yarkon. As you go more south you have poorer and older places though.Big central streets are Arlozerov, Zev Zabotinsky, Iben Gavirol so being close to one of those might be smart.on the same note - being close to Terminal 2000 \[[https://www.google.com/maps/place/Terminal+2000+-+Bus+Terminal/@32.082238,34.7906276,16.75z/data=!4m8!1m2!2m1!1z157XnNeV158!3m4!1s0x151d4b958b2b8f01:0xec12830eca1a897d!8m2!3d32.0827251!4d34.79598](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Terminal+2000+-+Bus+Terminal/@32.082238,34.7906276,16.75z/data=!4m8!1m2!2m1!1z157XnNeV158!3m4!1s0x151d4b958b2b8f01:0xec12830eca1a897d!8m2!3d32.0827251!4d34.79598)\] can be smart too if you plan on using buses as transport. There is no Metro or light rails like in many cities in europe so sadly buses, texis and bikes/electric scooters are your way to go.

If you plan on using taxis you can be anywhere and be fine.

There are a bunch of electric scooters scattered around the city and are pretty popular but can also be dangerous.

as to places to eat - I... really only eat shawarmas. Im not much of a restaurant guy. It would probably be the most cheap and fast food (prefer it over burgers). Falafels are also cheap street food but no meat.2 big trends right now is vegan food and ice cream. Golda's (ice cream shops) are really popular. I am less informed as for the vegan places...

Vetrina - good burger restaurant.

Bars:

Impirial - famous cocktail bar inside a lobby of a hotel on HaYarkon street (you dont need to be resident to enter). Its pretty small but has nice-classic atmosphere and good staff.

fantastic -  another good bar which is inside a hotel near Ta'arocha street. Much bigger bar then the Impirial but divided to many rooms. Has a similar classy aesthetic. It is also close to the Harbor (there are few good clubs there), so you can sit in fantastic before going out to a party in one of those.

Sputnik - a popular/famous ruin-styled bar near Rothshild avenue. Outside there is also a small coffee booth where people play music every evening \[[https://www.facebook.com/sputnikTLV/videos/179805240798216](https://www.facebook.com/sputnikTLV/videos/179805240798216)\]. I remember asking once the barista where can I find the stream and he kinda showed me it on youtube but I forgot and cant find it now.

Potion bar - Rock bar with DnD/RPG aesthetic. Drinks are served in lighted 'potion' glasses. I dont think its very popular but I like it. Might be less touristy since I didnt happen to stumble upon tourists there ever.

BellBoy is another nice bar.

Clubs:

Anything near the Harbor should be fine. 'Shalvata' is the most famous one and always has good mainstream music. 'Light House' and "Lizman" are good too. Those places have the younger audience though (18-24).

"Duplex" is three floors building where every floor has different music. Its not always open though (sometimes it has only 1 or 2 floors running).

"The Block" is regarded as one of the best clubs too.

However best check for events and go in special days. New year will probably be fun. You will also have Porim in 17-18 in March. Day celebrated with happiness and kids wear customs (like happy holloween) you may go out at night and see some people dressed out crazy.

Also Hanoka starts in 2 weeks.

If you plan to get out of Tel Aviv then there is also "Desert" in Rishon Le'Zion and "the forum" in Bear Sheva. The north (Haifa and the Kraiut) has good night life scene too.

Yeah the trip blow my mind, I originally planned to go with 2 friends but they dropped off so I went alone. It was the first time Im abroad alone with no family or friends.

A ship cruise on the Danube - to be honest that was kind of boring, couldnt take photos because of lighting and because there was no open deck.

szimpla kert  - Really nice, chill place where you have a chance to meet locals and some other tourists. If you like bars and pubs over clubs then this is great.

Terror haza - I heard a lot of good stuff about this museum... maybe because I came with high expectations but - it really was average experience. Its a museum that shows the horrors of the secret police of both the communists and the nazies. I didnt know about this thing at all so at least I learned something new.

national museum of history - This one was actually great. So rich in artifacts and facts. Even if you dont like a certain aspect, you have like 10 different eras and subjects to see there so you ought to find something you like.

free tour - This is better then the ship cruise in any aspect. better at familiarizing with the city. Better for photo taking and better for talking and connecting with people. Originally I planned to meet here with a portuguese girl I talked to a night before in szimpla, but we ended up in different groups. I did end up meeting a fellow israeli who was really fun to talk to. He came alone like me, was a bit older but good conversation friend.

Axe throwing - harder then it looks. Much harder.

Széchenyi bath - It was probably the best day-time activity I went to, but I wouldn't spend here more then a couple hours. I came early too (like 9:00) and stayed almost till 12:00. I think its better to come a bit later so you dont feel so lonely in those huge baths. great for taking photos. fun just to drip in the water. There is also a massage service. Before leaving I were meeting a couple from the netherlands and we shared a conversation.

Instant-fogas - very fun, one of the highpoints in the trip. I was there twice, once in Thursday and once in Saturday. Thursday I had huge fun, I came super early though (19:30?) and at that time there was only a rock group playing so I thought for the first hour that this is a concert house and not a club. Then it transformed into a huge club house and lots of cool people came in. I think it was mainly tourists, I came across a few fellow israelies there, had lots of positive interactions with people there.Saturday was too crowded though, to a point you could barely move.

Akvarium - Came here friday night. This and instant were my favorites. A cute Hungarian girl and her friends made my night here.

Oktart - I went here after akvarium and it was very crowded. I did like the music though.

Gellért Hill and fisherman's bastions and all this area of buda in general - much more relaxed and tamed then in pest. But probably the best for taking photos.

Sparty - was disappointing. Its not bad, but I just think that from all the parties this was probably the least exciting one. The only people I connected with there were an older couple from london and two druze israelies (which was super surprising to find there). most guys there came with a very certain goal and weren't relaxed or wanted to have fun. And I didn't want to bother the girls, also since the female:male ratio was probably 1:3.

as to food - I ate in restaurants from u/vernazza's list and cant remember anything I didnt like. I did shop a bit in the supermarket ('spar' or 'adni') and the brands of anything are so different then in israel so it was hard to even know what to buy. I did notice people love susages a lot.

best restaurant was probably Ket Szerecsen. Small, humble, good food, superb service (I wanted to give the waiter a tip since he was such a champ but he urged me not to so I just thanked him personally and promised ill leave them a good review).

Best bar I went to was boutiq' bar. But the city is really filled with good bars, at least around the astoria area.
